Cleandridas (b. 500 BCE) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, active in Global, known for his military leadership and strategic command. As a key figure in the Hellenistic period, Cleandridas played a significant role in shaping the administrative structures of various city-states, including Athens and Sparta. His legacy can be seen in the continued development of civic governance and military tactics in the ancient Mediterranean. The historian Plutarch noted that Cleandridas was 'a man of great courage and cunning, who had a natural talent for leadership and a deep understanding of the art of war.' In the centuries following his death, Cleandridas's reputation as a skilled military commander and administrator endured, with many historians and biographers hailing him as one of the most important figures of his time. The rediscovery of Cleandridas's works in the 19th century sparked a renewed interest in his life and achievements, with scholars and historians seeking to better understand the context and significance of his writings.

Cleandridas's contributions to the development of civic governance and military tactics had a lasting impact on the ancient Mediterranean world. His strategic command and leadership skills were studied and emulated by military leaders and politicians for centuries, with many historians noting that his legacy can be seen in the development of modern military doctrine and civic governance structures. The archaeological discovery of Cleandridas's tomb in the 20th century provided valuable insights into the life and achievements of this important historical figure, further solidifying his place in the annals of history.
